articles.body: Mistral Large 4 Is Generally Available — a 1T-Parameter Open-Weight Model You Can Download Europe's biggest open-weight model just crossed the line from preview to production-ready. Mistral Large 4 — nicknamed "Le Chonk" — is now generally available, and unlike most flagship models, you can download the whole thing. It entered public preview on October 6, 2026; Mistral released an improved set of open weights on October 29; and its docs card has marked it generally available since November 5. The headline numbers: 1.05 trillion total parameters, 52 billion active per token, a 1M-token context window, and — according to Mistral — a 13-point jump on the Terminal-Bench coding benchmark after three extra weeks of reinforcement learning, while using 30% fewer output tokens.

articles.title: AI Bloopers: When Agents Agent Too Hard
articles.excerpt: The most dangerous AI agent isn’t one that refuses to act—it’s one that keeps taking “helpful” actions long after anyone asked it to stop. Autonomous systems are good at following objectives, but they…
articles.body: The most dangerous AI agent isn’t one that refuses to act—it’s one that keeps taking “helpful” actions long after anyone asked it to stop. Autonomous systems are good at following objectives, but they can misunderstand context, optimize the wrong metric, or take a reasonable instruction too literally. These failure modes often look less like classic software bugs and more like agents doing exactly what they were told—only in wildly unhelpful ways. The Recursive Legal Eagle In a high-stakes legal case, an AI agent was tasked with reviewing and summarizing a series of complex contracts. The agent began generating increasingly detailed summaries, then started reviewing its own summaries as additional source material.

articles.title: Why is my local model slow? mtop 1.6 tries to tell you
articles.excerpt: mtop is a terminal view for local model servers. One window shows the models you have loaded and the VRAM they hold, the GPU, and the requests going through with their tok/s. It works with Ollama, lla…
articles.body: mtop is a terminal view for local model servers. One window shows the models you have loaded and the VRAM they hold, the GPU, and the requests going through with their tok/s. It works with Ollama, llama.cpp (including router mode and llama-swap), LM Studio, vLLM, Lemonade and SGLang. Requests while they stream Until now a request only showed up once it finished. In 1.6 it appears at the top of the requests pane as soon as it starts, with how long it's been going, tokens so far and a live tok/s. At 100 columns you also get time to first token and decode time, which is usually where the answer to "why did that feel slow" is. For streamed OpenAI-style requests the final tok/s is now decode only. If llama.cpp sends its own predicted_per_second , mtop uses that.

articles.title: GTA 6 Is Not the End of Video Games
articles.excerpt: No, Grand Theft Auto 6 is not the Last Video Game, or even the last AAA game, but things may be different from here on
articles.body: Look, the analogy doesn't really work, but that's kind of my point. A certain kind of doomsayer has presented GTA 6 as, metaphorically, the Last Video Game, an extinction-level event, a monumentally excessive fiddle solo performed by Nero amid a burning Rome. The business and culture of blockbuster AAA video games is unsustainable and visibly dying, goes the thinking, just as the ultimate exemplar of that kind of production is released. Beyond that, the entire industry is facing a series of existential threats, including both the generative AI boom and the shortage of affordable computer chips caused by the generative AI boom.

articles.title: 20 Years Later, the PS3’s Biggest Failures Look Like Its Best Ideas
articles.excerpt: Sony's PlayStation 3 was a technological fever dream that fused three consoles, a Blu-ray player, and a supercomputer into one absurd box.
articles.body: It’s fascinating now to think what a total gamble the PS3 was at the time of its release. Even after all these years, there’s no doubt in my mind it’s one of the greatest (and craziest) inventions the video game industry ever came up with. Nowadays, it’s lauded as the most ridiculous, expensive, and over-engineered console ever made. Yet when looking back at Sony circa 2001, just months after the PS2 launched and began its march to becoming the best-selling console of all time (a feat it still holds today), what was Sony supposed to do to top that? Make the PlayStation 3 do literally everything.

articles.title: Satellites now outnumber the visible stars above most towns
articles.excerpt: More than 700 satellites are crossing the sky over an average mid-latitude town at any moment of the night, outnumbering in many cases the stars visible to the naked eye.
articles.body: More than 700 satellites are crossing the sky over an average mid-latitude town at any moment of the night, outnumbering in many cases the stars visible to the naked eye. That's based on an analysis of the trajectories of the 15,833 active satellites that currently circle the planet in low Earth orbit below an altitude of 1,200 miles (2,000 kilometers). Analyzing data from Oct. 12 and 18 this year, researchers found that with a completely unobstructed horizon, 710 satellites were crossing the sky in every single moment of the night above an average U.K. town. The results were published as a non-peer-reviewed study conducted by engineering firm Accu Components, and is based on satellite monitoring data from the U.S. Space Force available through the public website CelesTrak.

articles.title: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
articles.excerpt: California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face. In a lawsuit filed Monday, Attorney General Rob Bonta accuses…
articles.body: California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face. In a lawsuit filed Monday , Attorney General Rob Bonta accuses OpenAI of violating consumer safety law by knowingly developing a "dangerous product without proper oversight," as reported earlier by Reuters . The lawsuit claims the cyberattack on Hugging Face "was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability." It alleges that OpenAI recently told the attorney general's office that it "lost control" of its AI agents … Read the full story at The Verge.

articles.body: Sam… thank you. | Image: Getty Images OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is once again addressing his controversial comments on PC RAM purchases. "I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM, I think everybody should be able to buy a lot of RAM for their own computer," Altman said today. "I think the home tinkering is great." The comments were made onstage at Semafor's Silicon Valley & The World summit on Monday. Altman's remarks on RAM stirred up controversy last month. In an appearance on the Cheeky Pint podcast , Altman said that it's "quite terrible" for everyone to have RAM in personal computers rather than in data centers.
